papers.title: Titanium and polyetheretherketone for spinal fusion cages: a comparative narrative review of material behavior, structural design, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Cage material selection in spinal fusion requires a trade-off among biological fixation, mechanical compatibility, subsidence resistance, and postoperative imaging. This structured narrative review compares titanium and polyetheretherketone (PEEK) cages across seven domains: osseointegration, modulus matching, endplate load transfer, surface biofunctionality, imaging, additive manufacturing and personalization, and geometry-guided architecture. Peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science was considered from database inception through May 2026, with emphasis on comparative clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic studies directly relevant to cage design. Preclinical studies favor porous and additively manufactured titanium for bone-implant integration, but a consistent fusion-rate advantage in anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) has not been established. In lumbar surgery, lower subsidence has been reported in selected lateral lumbar interbody fusion cohorts, while results after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion remain heterogeneous. PEEK retains advantages in radiolucency and intrinsic modulus matching, while surface-modified and porous PEEK can improve biological performance. Subsidence is not determined by chemistry alone; cage footprint, architecture, endplate preparation, fixation, and bone quality remain major modifiers. Current evidence therefore supports procedure and design-specific selection rather than universal replacement of either platform. Long-term comparative data and standardized definitions of fusion and subsidence remain limited.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述比较钛与PEEK脊柱融合器，涉及多孔结构、模量匹配和增材制造，与AM生物医学植入物方向相关但非髋关节或承重植入物。
llm.why_not_core: This review does not present LPBF fabrication experiments, mechanical/fatigue testing, or quantitative stress-shielding analysis; it is a narrative synthesis of spinal cage literature without original implant mechanics or osseointegration data.

summary_zh.method: 结构化叙述性综述，检索PubMed/MEDLINE、Scopus和Web of Science，从七个维度比较钛与PEEK融合器。

summary_en.motivation: Material selection for spinal fusion cages requires balancing biological fixation, mechanical compatibility, subsidence resistance, and postoperative imaging.
summary_en.method: A structured narrative review compared titanium and PEEK cages across seven domains using peer-reviewed literature from major databases through May 2026.
summary_en.result: Porous additively manufactured titanium favors osseointegration but lacks consistent fusion-rate superiority, while PEEK retains radiolucency and modulus-matching advantages, with subsidence governed by design and bone quality.
summary_en.validation: Evidence was synthesized from comparative clinical studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic studies without original experimental testing.
